purpose: Four 2x2 atlases for sixteen geographically specific ending scenes; consumed in runtime source rectangles without modifying image pixels.
prompts: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production-ready high-detail pixel-art background atlas for a Taiwan arcade driving game's ending scenes. Create ONE clean 2×2 atlas: FOUR equal wide landscape panels, zero gutters, zero borders, no text or lettering, no logos, no UI, no player characters or cars. Overall landscape ratio approximately 2:1, panels likewise approximately 2:1. Every panel is a continuous richly illustrated environment with natural perspective and layered depth, hand-placed-looking small crisp pixel clusters, 32-bit arcade/SNK travel-poster sophistication, saturated but tasteful colors, strong warm sun/cool shadow contrast, readable shadow details, delicate atmospheric distance, intricate realistic geographical shapes interpreted as polished pixel art, never flat polygon blocks or crude chunky minimalism. Pixel art not a 3D render, not a photograph. All four have low eye-level scenic overlook composition. Reserve the bottom 25% of EACH panel for an EMPTY broad level paved scenic arrival bay / safe roadside pullout, with restrained asphalt texture, natural shadows and a low curb separating it from landscape; this is where the game will later composite a rear-view car centered horizontally at 35% of panel width. The view beyond the bay is the location. Main landmark is in middle/right, not obscured by foreground. Keep all essential landmarks fully inside their own panel, no overflow across panel boundaries. Top-left can hold a small game label later, so no vital landmarks there. High-end HD-2D visual mood, beautiful detailed cohesive light, trees with sculpted foliage, miniature people forbidden, parked vehicles forbidden. EXACT PANEL CONTENTS in reading order: TOP LEFT = Taipei City's Xinyi district at blue hour: unmistakable TAIPEI 101, a tall teal tiered bamboo pagoda-like skyscraper with EIGHT stacked outward flaring modules and one slender spire; surrounding smaller modern towers, warm lit windows, detailed Taiwanese urban avenue/shopfront edges, dense layered skyline with distant mountain silhouettes; no Kaohsiung 85 tower, no seaport cranes. TOP RIGHT = Yehliu Geopark in Wanli, New Taipei: Queen's Head sandstone formation a slender eroded neck and broad head silhouette, distinctive honey-gold mushroom sandstone rocks and honeycomb weathering over low wave-cut coastal rock terraces, sapphire ocean, warm late-afternoon sunlight. No skyline or city. BOTTOM LEFT = Sun Moon Lake Shuishe, Yuchi, Nantou: quiet enclosed emerald-blue mountain lake with several successive lush forested ridges, a tasteful wooden lakeside pier and small moored excursion boats, small refined waterside visitor architecture, warm reflected light. Absolutely not open ocean, no seaport cranes or coastal skyscrapers. BOTTOM RIGHT = Wuling at Hehuanshan, Ren'ai, Nantou: high open mountain pass, huge layered craggy blue-grey peaks and rolling alpine arrow-bamboo grass slopes, small unlettered natural stone pass marker on right, cloud sea tucked between mountains, crisp bright alpine sun. NO jungle palms, NO lake, no snow resort, no buildings dominating. Landmark and landforms must be distinctly identifiable and accurate. All 4 spaces are calm celebratory end-of-journey views.
